findings.title: Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock causes thundering herd
findings.body: GetWebAssets does a fast-path check under RLock and if it misses acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu in write mode, but it never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock. If N goroutines concurrently observe a nil cache before the first load finishes, each will queue on the write lock and each will re-read assets-manifest.json/CDN and overwrite the global. The consequence is redundant disk/network I/O on cold start, wasted work, and different callers getting different pointers when one shared load would suffice.

findings.title: Exclusive lock held across file and network I/O blocks all readers
findings.body: GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu with Lock and defers Unlock, so the exclusive lock is held across readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN, which perform file-system reads and HTTP fetches plus GetContentDeliveryURL. While the writer holds the lock, every other caller blocks even for RLock fast-path cache hits. In Dev mode every call takes the write lock, so concurrent requests fully serialize on disk I/O. This adds latency and contention; the load should happen outside the lock with a second check/singleflight and the lock held only to publish the result.

findings.title: Failed load overwrites good cache with nil
findings.body: GetWebAssets unconditionally executes entryPointAssetsCache = result even when the load failed and result is nil with err non-nil. In Dev mode the read bypasses the cache but the write still overwrites it, so one transient failure reading assets-manifest.json discards the previously good cached EntryPointAssets shared by all goroutines. Subsequent callers then see a nil cache and fail or must reload until a later success. The global should only be updated on success (err == nil and result != nil) to preserve the last good value.
